note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Perform wet hair styling and roller placement

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why do you ask the client how long she wants her set to last and where she is going?
options: To choose the roller size, the set pattern and the products
To decide whether she should pay before or after the service
To know which other stylist can finish the set if you are busy
To work out how many hair pins you can save for later

questions.stem: Why does a wet set hold the hair in a new shape?
options: The water and the rollers change the hair's protein for good
The setting lotion glues each hair to the next one
Bonds broken by water re-form in the new shape as the hair dries
The heat of the hood dryer melts the cuticle into a new shape

questions.stem: Why does a roller set drop or go frizzy quickly in humid weather?
options: The hair grows faster in humid weather and loses the curl
The hair takes in moisture from the air and loses its set
Humid air makes the hairspray turn into a strong glue
Humidity makes the rollers' marks show up in the hair

questions.stem: What condition should the hair be in before you start a wet set?
options: Dry, with the old style still in it
Clean, detangled and evenly damp
Soaking wet and full of conditioner
Oily, so that the rollers slide in

questions.stem: Part of the hair dries out while you are still winding the set. What should you do?
options: Dampen it again with a water spray before winding it
Wind it dry, as it will set the same way as wet hair
Put extra setting lotion on the rollers already done
Leave that part out and blow-dry it at the end

questions.stem: Which rollers are best for a wet set on relaxed hair, to give a smooth, full finish?
options: Smooth plastic rollers held with pins
Self-grip rollers on dry, straight hair
Heated rollers straight from the case
Small perm rods wound very tightly

questions.stem: What is the main use of flexi-rods?
options: To straighten curly hair by pulling it smooth
To make spiral curls by winding along the hair
To hold a French pleat in place at the back
To protect the ears under the hood dryer

questions.stem: Why do you use end papers when winding short or fine ends on a roller?
options: To add colour to the ends while the hair is drying
To make the hair dry faster under the hood dryer
To hold the ends smooth so they do not bend or frizz
To soak up the extra setting lotion from the roots

questions.stem: How should roller pins be put in to hold a roller?
options: Pushed in hard so that the point rests firmly on the scalp
Through the hair only, with no roller to hold
Across the top of the roller, without going through it at all
Through the roller to its base, without touching the scalp

questions.stem: What is a hair net used for during a roller set?
options: To keep the setting lotion off the client's face
To hold the rollers in place while the hair dries
To stop the hood dryer getting too hot
To make the curls come out tighter

questions.stem: Which roller size gives the tightest curl?
options: The largest roller you have
A medium roller wound loosely
Any roller, as size makes no difference
A small roller

questions.stem: A client wants soft, loose waves and plenty of volume. Which should you choose?
options: Large rollers
Small perm rods
Thin flexi-rods
Tiny pin curls

questions.stem: What does setting lotion do?
options: Helps the set hold its shape and last longer
Washes out the old products left in the hair
Straightens the hair before it is wound on rollers
Colours grey hair while the set dries

questions.stem: How should setting lotion be applied?
options: Only at the roots, rubbed firmly into the scalp
Only on the ends, after all the rollers are in
Poured straight from the bottle onto the crown
Evenly through towel-dried hair, root to ends

questions.stem: Why should you not use too much gel or setting product on a wet set?
options: It can leave the hair stiff, flaky and slow to dry
It makes the rollers slide off the hair too easily
It causes the hair to change colour as it dries
It makes the curls drop out in the first hour

questions.stem: Which product would suit a flexi-rod set on natural, coily hair?
options: A heavy grease rubbed onto the scalp
A curl cream or setting foam
A strong hairspray before winding
A clarifying shampoo left in

questions.stem: What is the 'base' in roller setting?
options: The setting lotion put on before winding
The end of the hair that goes on the roller first
The bottom row of rollers at the nape
The section of scalp the roller sits on

questions.stem: How big should the base section for a roller be?
options: Twice as wide as the roller and twice as deep
As large as possible, so fewer rollers are needed
About half the length of the roller, any depth
About as long and as wide as the roller itself

questions.stem: Which roller placement gives the most volume at the roots?
options: Off base
Half-off base
On base
Under the base

questions.stem: For a half-off base roller, how is the hair held from the head while you wind?
options: Flat down against the head
Pulled down 45 degrees
Pulled up and over its base
Straight out, at 90 degrees

questions.stem: When would you use an off-base roller?
options: When the client wants the most lift at the roots
When the hair is too short to reach round the roller at all
When the hair is very wet and heavy
When the client wants little volume but curl at the ends

questions.stem: Why are rollers often placed in a 'brick' pattern, like bricks in a wall?
options: So that the set dries faster at the crown and in the middle
So that there are no gaps or straight parting lines in the set
So that the client can sleep comfortably with the rollers in
So that fewer rollers are needed for long, thick hair

questions.stem: Why should the sections for a roller set be clean and even?
options: So that the client cannot see the parting lines in the mirror
So that the stylist uses up less of the setting lotion
So that each roller holds the same amount of hair for an even set
So that the rollers can later be taken out without using a comb

questions.stem: When winding hair on a roller, how should the ends be placed?
options: Bent back on themselves so they curl more tightly
Left out of the roller to dry straight and flat
Spread smoothly across the roller with no bends
Twisted together in a point at the centre

questions.stem: Why should the hair be wound with even tension?
options: So that the client feels the pull and knows it is working
So that the curl is smooth and even from root to end
So that the roller can be placed as far off base as it can
So that the hair is stretched until it is longer for good

questions.stem: What can happen if rollers are wound too tightly?
options: The set will dry far too quickly under the dryer
The hair may break and the scalp may become sore
The curls will come out much looser than wanted
The setting lotion will turn white on the hair

questions.stem: What is 'directional' winding?
options: Placing rollers to follow the way the hair will be styled
Winding every single roller towards the client's face
Winding all rollers from the nape up to the crown
Placing all of the rollers in one single straight line

questions.stem: What is the difference between spiral winding and croquignole winding?
options: Spiral winding is for short hair; croquignole is for wigs only
Spiral winding uses heat; croquignole uses only cold water
Spiral winds along the strand; croquignole winds ends to roots
Spiral uses rollers; croquignole uses only the fingers

questions.stem: What are the three parts of a pin curl?
options: The root, the shaft and the tip
The base, the stem and the circle
The clip, the pin and the net
The wave, the ridge and the trough

questions.stem: Which part of a pin curl gives it direction and movement?
options: The stem
The clip
The end paper
The parting

questions.stem: How should a pin curl be clipped so that the clip does not leave a mark?
options: With the clip pressed hard right across both the stem and base
With a large roller clip pushed into the scalp
With two clips crossing over the top of the circle
Through the circle at the base, without crossing the stem

questions.stem: Which type of pin curl gives curls of the same size from end to end, for an even wave?
options: A closed-centre curl
A no-stem curl
An open-centre curl
A curl with a very long stem

questions.stem: What are finger waves?
options: S-shaped waves formed with the fingers and a comb on wet hair
Waves made by twisting the hair around the fingers while dry
Waves made with a hot tong pressed on with the fingertips
Waves cut into the hair with scissors held in the fingers

questions.stem: What is the raised line between two finger waves called?
options: The trough
The stem
The base
The ridge

questions.stem: Why are perm rods sometimes used for a wet set on natural hair, with no perm solution?
options: To relax the curl pattern for good without a chemical
To give small, defined curls that dry into a neat set
To add length by stretching each strand around the rod
To protect the hair from heat while it is pressed

questions.stem: Before a flexi-rod set on natural hair, why must the hair be fully detangled?
options: So that the rods can be wound with fewer sections
So that the hair takes longer to dry under the hood
So that less setting product is needed on each rod
So that each curl is smooth and the hair does not snap

questions.stem: What is a 'wrap' (wrap set) on relaxed hair?
options: A head scarf tied over the hair to protect it from rain
A plait wound around the head and pinned at the crown
Wet hair combed smoothly round the head and dried flat
A towel wrapped round the head after the shampoo

questions.stem: How should the client be placed under the hood dryer?
options: With the hood resting firmly on her rollers to hold them
With the dryer set to its hottest heat to save time
With her ears pressed against the side of the hood
Seated comfortably, hood at the right height, heat checked

questions.stem: Why should you protect the client's ears during hood drying?
options: The ears can get too hot and burn under the hood
The ears make the rollers slip down towards the neck
The ears stop the hot air from reaching the nape
The ears are where the setting lotion collects

questions.stem: How do you check that a roller set is completely dry?
options: Ask the client if her scalp feels hot under the dryer
Unwind a roller at the crown or nape and feel the hair
Look at the rollers to see if they have changed colour
Wait 10 minutes after the timer, whatever the hair type

questions.stem: Why should a set be left to cool before the rollers are taken out?
options: So that the rollers are cool enough to put away
So that the client can pay while the hair cools
So that the curls set firmly and last longer
So that the dryer can cool down for the next client

questions.stem: What is the best way to remove the rollers?
options: Gently, starting at the nape and working up, without pulling
Quickly, pulling each roller straight down off the hair
All at once, by brushing them out of the hair with a paddle brush
While the hair is still damp, so it is easier to style

questions.stem: After the rollers are out, how do you blend the curls into the finished style?
options: Wash the hair again and leave it to dry on its own
Pull each curl straight with a fine comb until smooth
Brush through gently, then shape and back-comb as needed
Spray each curl with water to make it softer and longer

questions.stem: After a roller set, how should the rollers be cleaned?
options: Shake the hair off and put them back in the box
Remove the hair, wash, disinfect and dry them
Leave them in the sun for a day to kill germs
Wipe them with a dry towel at the end of the week

questions.stem: The client says the hood dryer feels too hot. What should you do?
options: Tell her it needs to be hot or the set will not dry
Give her a fan to hold while she sits under it
Turn the heat down at once and check her scalp and ears
Lift the hood up a little and leave it on the same heat

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do we call a bent or crooked end on a curl, caused by poor winding?
What is the name for the thin piece of hair taken from a section to wind on one roller?
What is the name of the comb with a long, thin, pointed handle used to part clean sections?
Which bonds in the hair are broken by water and then re-form as the hair dries in its new shape?
What is the name of a pin curl that stands up from the scalp on its base, to give volume?
What one word describes the amount of lift and body a set has at the roots?
What is the name for brushing out and shaping the curls into the finished style after a set?
What word describes coily hair drawing up and looking shorter as it dries?
What is the name for the highest part of the head, at the top towards the back?
What is the name of a spiral pattern in which the hair grows out from one point, often at the crown?
A set needs 32 rollers. You have put in 18. How many more rollers are needed?
A client goes under the dryer at 11:20 a.m. for 45 minutes. At what time will the drying finish?
What are placed over the client's ears to protect them from the heat of the hood dryer?
What soft rollers can a client sleep in comfortably at home?
What is the name of the clip with two prongs used to hold pin curls in place?

essays.stem: Mrs Brown has relaxed, shoulder-length hair. She wants a roller set for a family wedding in July and needs it to last through hot, humid weather. Explain the choices you would make, from the shampoo to her aftercare, so that the set lasts, and say why.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with a consultation to agree the style and check her hair and scalp. I would shampoo with a gentle shampoo and use a light conditioner, because heavy conditioners can make the set drop. I would blot the hair and apply a firm-hold setting lotion evenly, as the maker says, because it helps the hydrogen bonds hold the new shape. I would use smooth plastic rollers a little smaller than usual, as the curl will relax in humid air, and wind with smooth ends and even tension. I would dry the set completely under the hood dryer, checking the crown and nape, because any damp hair will drop quickly. I would let it cool fully before removing the rollers, so the curls set firmly. After dressing out, I would use a light hairspray that resists humidity. I would advise her to wrap the hair or wear a satin bonnet at night, keep a shower cap and umbrella handy, and avoid touching the curls too much.
markingPoints: Light conditioning and a firm-hold setting lotion, with the reason
Slightly smaller rollers and good winding, because the curl relaxes in humidity
Dries the set completely, checking the crown and nape
Lets the set cool fully before removing the rollers
Finishing spray and aftercare: wrap or satin bonnet at night, protect from damp air

essays.stem: Plan a full-head roller set for a client who wants volume on top and smooth ends curled under at the nape. Describe the roller sizes, the base placements and the pattern you would use, and say why.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation, shampoo and setting lotion, I would divide the hair into sections. On the top, from the front hairline to the crown, I would use large rollers set on base, with the hair held up and slightly forward over the base, so the roller sits right on it. This gives the most lift at the roots. On the crown and the upper sides I would use medium rollers, half-off base, holding the hair straight out at 90 degrees, to give medium volume that blends into the top. At the nape and lower sides, I would use smaller rollers set off base, with the hair held down, so there is little lift but the ends curl under smoothly. I would wind the rollers back and down, following the way the style will be dressed. I would place the back rollers in a brick pattern so there are no gaps or splits when the set is brushed out.
markingPoints: Large rollers on base on the top for the most volume
Medium rollers half-off base on the crown and upper sides
Smaller rollers off base at the nape for curl with little lift
Directional winding that follows the finished style
Brick pattern to avoid gaps or splits, with reasons given

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to wind one roller correctly, from taking the section to securing it.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that the hair is evenly damp and combed through, with setting lotion applied. With a tail comb I take a clean section about as long and as wide as the roller. I comb the hair smooth from the roots to the ends and hold it at the angle needed for the base placement: up and over the base for on base, straight out for half-off base, or down for off base. If the ends are short or fine, I fold an end paper over them. I place the roller under the ends and make sure the ends lie smooth and spread across it, with no bends. I wind the roller down towards the scalp with even, firm tension, keeping the hair spread across the width of the roller. When it reaches the base, I secure it with a roller pin pushed through the roller and into the base, without touching the scalp. I check that the client is comfortable.
markingPoints: Damp, combed hair; clean section about the size of the roller
Holds the hair at the right angle for the base placement
Ends smooth and spread on the roller, using an end paper if needed
Winds down with even, firm tension, the hair spread across the roller
Secures with a pin through the roller to the base without touching the scalp

essays.stem: Describe how to form and secure a row of flat pin curls, and explain how the length of the stem changes the result.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with damp hair combed smooth, with setting lotion. I part a row of even sections, such as squares or triangles, along the area to be curled. I comb one section smooth in the direction I want the curl to go. Holding the hair near the base, I wind the ends around my finger to make a smooth circle, keeping the ends inside, and slide the curl off my finger. I lay it flat on its base and secure it with a double-prong clip through the circle at the base, without crossing the stem, so that no mark is left. I repeat along the row, with all the curls going the same way. The stem decides how much movement the curl has. A no-stem curl sits right on its base and gives a firm, tight curl. A half-stem curl sits half off the base and gives more movement. A full-stem curl sits off the base and gives the most movement and the loosest result.
markingPoints: Damp, smooth hair with setting lotion, parted in even sections
Forms a smooth circle around the finger with the ends inside
Lays it flat and clips through the base without crossing the stem
Keeps all curls in the row going the same direction
Explains no-stem, half-stem and full-stem results correctly

essays.stem: Describe how to create finger waves on wet hair.
essays.modelAnswer: Finger waves suit hair that is at least a few centimetres long. After the shampoo, I apply a setting lotion or gel evenly while the hair is wet, and comb it smooth. I find the natural parting and comb the hair in the direction the first wave will go, following the head shape. I place my index finger just above where the first ridge will be, and comb the hair under it forward about 2 to 3 cm, then press the hair together between my finger and the comb to form a raised ridge. I move along the head, making the ridge in a smooth line. Then I comb the next section in the opposite direction and form the second ridge, making an S shape. I carry on down the head, keeping the waves an even width. I can finish the ends with pin curls. I put a net and ear protectors on and dry the waves under a hood dryer, then let them cool before removing the net.
markingPoints: Wet hair with setting lotion or gel, combed smooth from the parting
Uses the finger and comb to push the hair and form a raised ridge
Combs the next section the opposite way to make an S shape
Keeps waves even in width and follows the head shape
Dries under a hood with net and ear protection, and cools before removing

essays.stem: Describe how to do a flexi-rod or perm-rod wet set on natural, coily hair, from the shampoo to the finished style.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation and scalp check, I shampoo the hair in sections with a moisturising shampoo and condition it. I detangle each section gently with a wide-tooth comb, from the ends up to the roots, and keep the hair damp with a spray bottle. I apply a leave-in conditioner and a curl cream or setting foam to each small section and comb it smooth. I take sections about the width of the rod. For flexi-rods, I place the end of the hair on the rod and wind it smoothly along the strand towards the scalp, with even tension, then bend the ends of the rod to hold it. For perm rods, I wind from the ends to the roots and fasten the band without pressing on the hair. I dry the set fully under a hood dryer on a medium heat, which can take a long time, and let it cool. I remove the rods gently, separate the curls with oiled fingers and shape the style, allowing for shrinkage.
markingPoints: Shampoos, conditions and detangles gently in sections
Applies leave-in and a curl cream or setting foam to small sections
Winds smoothly with even tension and secures without crushing the hair
Dries completely under the hood and lets it cool
Removes gently, separates with oiled fingers and allows for shrinkage

essays.stem: Describe how to dry a roller set safely under a hood dryer, and how you would look after the client while she is under it.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the client sits down, I check the dryer: the plug, cable and hood must not be damaged, and it must work. I put a hair net over the rollers and place ear protectors or cotton wool over her ears. I seat her comfortably, with her back supported, and adjust the hood so that it covers the rollers without pressing on them. I set the heat and time to suit her hair, usually a medium heat, and ask her how it feels. I give her a magazine and water, and make sure her bag is safe. I check on her every 10 minutes or so, asking if the heat is comfortable, and turn it down at once if she feels too hot. When the time is up, I unwind one roller at the crown and one at the nape to check the hair is completely dry. If it is, I switch off the dryer, lift the hood and let the set cool before removing the rollers.
markingPoints: Checks the dryer before use
Uses a net and protects the ears
Seats the client comfortably, with the hood adjusted and a suitable heat
Checks on the client regularly and turns the heat down if needed
Checks dryness at the crown and nape and lets the set cool

essays.stem: Describe how to take out the rollers and dress out a set into a finished style.
essays.modelAnswer: I make sure the hair is completely dry and has cooled. I take out the pins first, then remove the rollers gently, starting at the nape and working up to the top, unwinding each one without pulling so that the curl is not stretched. I put the rollers and pins straight into a bowl to be cleaned. I let the curls sit for a moment. Then I brush through the hair gently with a bristle or cushion brush to blend the curls and remove the roller marks. I shape the hair with my hands and the brush into the style agreed at the consultation. For more height or hold, I back-comb lightly at the roots and smooth over the top. I check the balance from the front and sides in the mirror. I finish with a light hairspray or shine spray, protecting the client's face, and show her the back with a hand mirror. I give her advice on keeping the set, such as wrapping it at night.
markingPoints: Hair fully dry and cooled before removal
Removes pins and rollers gently from the nape upwards without pulling
Brushes through to blend curls and remove roller marks
Shapes, back-combs if needed and checks the balance
Finishes with product, shows the back and gives aftercare advice

essays.stem: Describe the main tools and equipment used for wet setting, and explain how to keep them clean and in good condition.
essays.modelAnswer: The main tools are a tail comb for clean sections, a wide-tooth comb for detangling, sectioning clips, rollers of different sizes, roller pins or picks, flexi-rods and perm rods for natural hair, end papers, double-prong clips for pin curls, a spray bottle of water, a hair net, ear protectors and a hood dryer. A bristle or cushion brush is used for dressing out. After each client, I remove all hair from the combs, rollers, rods and clips. I wash them in warm, soapy water and rinse them. I put them in a disinfectant solution for the contact time the maker gives, then rinse and dry them. I store them in a clean, covered container. I wash hair nets or throw away single-use ones, and throw away used end papers. I wipe the hood dryer with a suitable disinfectant when it is cool and unplugged, and report any fault. Bent pins or cracked rollers are thrown away, because they can catch the hair.
markingPoints: Names a good range of tools and what each is for
Removes hair, washes and rinses tools
Disinfects for the maker's contact time, then dries and stores covered
Throws away single-use items; cleans the dryer when cool and unplugged
Discards damaged tools and reports faults

essays.stem: Describe how to do a wrap set on shoulder-length relaxed hair, and the advice you would give the client to keep it.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation, I shampoo and condition the hair and blot it with a towel. I apply a setting lotion or wrap lotion evenly and comb it through with a wide-tooth comb, then a finer comb. I make a parting where the client wants it. Starting at the parting, I comb the hair smoothly in one direction around the head, following the head shape, keeping it flat and close to the scalp. I work all the way around, smoothing each part over the next so that the whole head is wrapped in a circle. I may place a large roller at the crown for height. I hold the hair in place with clips or a wrap strip, cover it with a net and protect the ears. I dry it fully under a hood dryer, let it cool, then comb it out and smooth it into a straight, swinging style. I advise the client to wrap the hair again every night with a satin scarf, and to keep it away from water and humid air.
markingPoints: Shampoo, condition and apply wrap or setting lotion evenly
Combs the hair smoothly round the head in one direction from the parting
Keeps the hair flat and smooth, secured with clips or a strip and a net
Dries fully under the hood, cools and combs out
Advises wrapping nightly with a satin scarf and avoiding water and humidity

practical1.title: Full-head roller set and dress out
practical1.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5 in the Centre's salon. Each member gives a full-head roller set to a training head or to a group partner or model who agrees. At least one client or training head in the group must have relaxed hair and one natural or textured hair that has been stretched. Each stylist plans the set first on a sketch of the head, showing the roller sizes and base placements, then applies setting lotion, winds the set with large rollers on base on top, half-off base on the crown and sides and off base at the nape, in a brick pattern at the back. The set is dried under a hood dryer, cooled, taken out and dressed into a finished style. Members take turns to photograph each other's work and to time the dryer. Photograph only the hair and work area, never faces, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group when every set is dressed out and the stations are clean.
materials: Training heads on clamps, or clients with clean, damp hair
Smooth plastic rollers in large, medium and small sizes
Tail combs, wide-tooth combs and sectioning clips
Setting lotion and a spray bottle of water
Bristle or cushion brushes, hairspray and a hand mirror
photos: The hair sectioned, with setting lotion applied
The finished set from the top, showing on-base rollers
The finished set from the back, showing the brick pattern
The set under the hood dryer, with net and ear protectors
The finished dressed-out style from the back and side
Rollers and tools cleaned and stations tidy
checklist: Planned the set to suit the hair and the result wanted
Kept the hair evenly damp and applied setting lotion evenly
Took clean, even sections about the size of each roller
Used the correct angle for on base, half-off base and off base
Wound with smooth ends and even tension, with no fish hooks
Placed the back rollers in a brick pattern with no gaps
Dried and cooled the set fully before removing the rollers
Dressed out a smooth, balanced finished style, then cleaned the tools
safety: Check each hood dryer before use and protect the client's ears
Ask live clients about heat and comfort every 10 minutes
Push roller pins through the roller only, never into the scalp
Keep the floor dry and clear of rollers, pins and cables

practical2.title: Finger waves and pin curls, and a flexi-rod set on textured hair
practical2.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5 in the Centre's salon. Part A: each member creates at least three finger-wave ridges on one side of a training head with wet hair, using setting gel, and finishes the ends with a row of flat pin curls clipped without marks. Part B: the group sets a training head with textured (coily) hair, or a group partner or model with natural hair who agrees, with flexi-rods. Each member detangles, applies product and winds at least two sections, and the group dries the set under a hood dryer. When it is dry and cool, each member takes down and separates the curls from the sections they wound. Members photograph each other's work at each stage. Photograph only the hair and work area, never faces, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group when the work is finished and the stations are clean.
materials: Training heads with long, wet straight or relaxed hair, on clamps
A training head with textured hair, or a client with natural hair
Setting gel or lotion, curl cream or setting foam, and leave-in conditioner
Fine combs, tail combs and wide-tooth combs
Flexi-rods in two or more sizes
Hair nets, ear protectors and a hood dryer
photos: The first finger-wave ridge being formed with the finger and comb
Three or more finished ridges on each training head
The row of pin curls at the ends
The textured hair detangled and sectioned for flexi-rods
The finished flexi-rod set before drying
The curls taken down and separated
checklist: Applied setting gel evenly and combed the hair smooth
Formed raised ridges with an even S shape that follows the head
Made smooth pin curls with the ends inside, clipped without crossing the stem
Detangled the textured hair gently from the ends to the roots
Wound flexi-rods smoothly with even tension and secured them neatly
Took down the dry, cooled set gently and separated the curls
Cleaned and disinfected the tools and left the station tidy
safety: Check the hood dryer before use and protect the ears of any live client
Fix training heads firmly in their clamps
Do not wind rods so tightly that they pull the scalp
Keep clips and rods off the floor and wipe up any spilled gel
